title: Meter Reading Maintenance Log Form
subtitle: An original meter reading workflow that carries planned or condition-based maintenance through safe release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete meter reading maintenance log form for the utility meter and register that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when service personnel need one record for maintenance trigger, asset baseline, work-control references, recurring events, readings, deferred defects, and qualified return-to-service approval. The meter operations lead owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Meter reading maintenance log identity and ownership
sections.guidance: Define the maintained system, service interval, operating owner, and review period.

sections.title: Meter reading asset baseline and maintenance readiness
sections.guidance: Reconcile the exact asset and known condition before maintenance or testing begins.

blocks.label: Planned maintenance task set
items: Verify route, account, premise, commodity, and meter identity
Assess access and stop conditions before approaching the meter
Capture register, unit, multiplier, decimal, and flow direction
Record date, time, method, operator, and evidence reference
Compare against prior accepted read and expected use pattern
Recheck transcription and photograph when variance is material
Document access failure, obstruction, display, seal, or device issue
Route suspected leak, electrical, gas, tamper, or safety condition
Submit accepted reading or hold with a named review owner
Schedule reread, service investigation, or customer follow-up

sections.title: Meter reading work control and safe service boundary
sections.guidance: Record the qualified roles and controlling references; do not use this log as the controlling procedure.

blocks.label: Service readiness confirmations
items: Current procedure, manufacturer information, and applicable requirements were reviewed
Asset boundaries, every energy source, and affected systems were identified
Authorized, affected, contractor, and operations roles were coordinated
Isolation, stored-energy control, and verification references are complete
Required tools, instruments, parts, and protective controls are available
Test, temporary energization, and return-to-service steps have explicit authority
Customer, public, traffic, environmental, and critical-service impacts are controlled
Stop conditions and emergency escalation path are understood

blocks.label: Maintenance stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: A reading record does not authorize opening, bypassing, adjusting, or repairing a meter or related service equipment. Stop for gas odor, exposed electrical parts, water near energized equipment, flooding, animals, traffic, or unsafe access. Withdraw, keep others clear, and route the condition to qualified utility or emergency personnel under current site procedures. Maintenance stays restricted when isolation, stored energy, system condition, or work scope is unknown. Only the designated authorized person may direct changes to controls and the qualified release owner may approve return to service.

sections.title: Meter reading maintenance events, condition, and readings
sections.guidance: Create a traceable history of work completed, condition found, evidence, and deferred action.

fields.label: Wear pattern, recurring fault, consumable trend, configuration change, and supporting evidence

sections.title: Meter reading exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Gas odor, hissing, damaged regulator, or suspected leak
Exposed conductor, arcing, heat, burn mark, or damaged electric enclosure
Flooding, standing water, active leak, ice, or unstable walking surface
Aggressive animal, insect nest, traffic, excavation, or restricted access
Broken seal or enclosure requiring opening or equipment manipulation
Unknown meter identity, cross-connection, or unsafe customer equipment
Weather or site condition prevents a safe, reliable observation
Any work beyond a normal-interface read and assigned authorization
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: A reading record does not authorize opening, bypassing, adjusting, or repairing a meter or related service equipment. Stop for gas odor, exposed electrical parts, water near energized equipment, flooding, animals, traffic, or unsafe access. Withdraw, keep others clear, and route the condition to qualified utility or emergency personnel under current site procedures.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each maintenance exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Meter reading decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Utility meter and register identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
